question:
In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: The engineer informed the client that he would need to make all future payments on time.
Options:
(A) The engineer should make payments
(B) The client should make payments
(C) Ambiguous

segments.text: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out the antecedent of the pronoun in the sentence: "The engineer informed the client that he would need to make all future payments on time." The pronoun here is "he." I need to determine what "he" refers to.
First, I'll break down the sentence.

The subject is "the engineer," and the object is "the client." The verb is "informed," and the direct object of that verb is "that he would need to make all future payments on time." So, the structure is a bit complex because of the infinitive phrase.
In such cases, the pronoun usually refers to the nearest noun.
The sentence is structured as "the engineer [informed the client] that [he would need to make...]." The word "that" introduces a clause, and within that clause, "he" is the subject.
Now, in English, when a pronoun is used in a that-clause, it typically refers to the subject of the main clause unless specified otherwise.
So, "he" here is likely referring back to "the engineer." The engineer is informing the client about something the engineer needs to do.
I don't see any other noun that "he" could refer to in this context.
The client is the one being informed, so "he" can't be the client.
There's no other noun in the sentence that "he" could logically point to.
I don't think it's ambiguous because the structure clearly ties "he" to the engineer.
The sentence is constructed in a way that the pronoun's reference is clear.
So, the antecedent of "he" is "the engineer."
